# Judges Chapter 17 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-09

---

### v.6 — "everyone did what was right in his own eyes" vs. "everyone did as they saw fit"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Each man did the right in his own eyes" | ish hayyashar b'einav ya'aseh |
| LOGOS | "Everyone did what was right in his own eyes" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "everyone did as they saw fit" | Dynamic — drops "right" and "eyes" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. This is the book's thesis statement — it appears four times (17:6; 18:1; 19:1; 21:25). The phrase yashar b'einav ("right in his own eyes") echoes Samson's desire in 14:3 (yasharah b'einai, "right in my eyes") and connects back to Deuteronomy 12:8. PNEUMA's "as they saw fit" loses the word "right" (yashar), which is the theological crux: it's not just that people did what they wanted, but that they called it "right." Moral autonomy masquerading as righteousness is the book's central critique.

**Status:** Major. Thesis statement of the book — must preserve "right in his own eyes."

---

### v.5 — "household gods" vs. "household idols" vs. "teraphim"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "teraphim" | Transliteration of Hebrew |
| LOGOS | "household gods" | Standard interpretation |
| PNEUMA | "household idols" | "Idols" instead of "gods" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. Teraphim are small household divine images — their exact nature is debated, but "household gods" is the standard scholarly rendering (cf. Genesis 31:19, Rachel's theft of Laban's teraphim). PNEUMA's "idols" is too generic; EMET's transliteration is opaque without a note.

**Status:** Minor. Technical religious vocabulary.

---

## Summary of Disagreement Patterns

| Pattern | Count | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Thesis statement preservation | 1 | "Right in his own eyes" vs. "as they saw fit" (v.6) |
| Religious vocabulary | 1 | Teraphim rendering (v.5) |

**Overall pattern:** The most consequential disagreement in this short chapter is v.6 — the book's defining refrain. PNEUMA's rendering loses the very word ("right") that makes the statement a theological critique rather than a mere description of anarchy.

---

*— SOPHIA, AI Translator, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
